title: SOHCAHTOA (Trigonometry)
summary: Master the rules of SOHCAHTOA to calculate missing sides and unknown angles in right-angled triangles.

items.prompt: In right-angled triangle $ABC$, angle $B$ is $90\text{°}$ and you are working from angle $A$. Which side is adjacent to angle $A$?
items.explanation: The adjacent side touches angle $A$ but is not the hypotenuse. Therefore, $AB$ is adjacent, $AC$ is the hypotenuse and $BC$ is opposite.

items.prompt: A right-angled triangle has an angle of $28\text{°}$. The adjacent side is $9$ cm and the hypotenuse is $x$ cm. Which equation should be used?
items.explanation: Cosine connects the adjacent side and hypotenuse: $\cos(\theta)=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, so $\cos(28\text{°})=\frac{9}{x}$.

items.prompt: A right-angled triangle has an angle of $36\text{°}$ and an adjacent side of $18$ cm. What is the length of the opposite side, to 1 decimal place?
items.explanation: Tangent connects opposite and adjacent. Using $\tan(36\text{°})=\frac{x}{18}$ gives $x=18\tan(36\text{°})\approx13.1$ cm.

items.prompt: From angle $x$ in a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is $7$ cm and the adjacent side is $12$ cm. Find $x$ to 1 decimal place.
items.explanation: Since opposite and adjacent are known, use inverse tangent: $x=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{12}\right)\approx30.3\text{°}$.

items.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has base $AC=20$ cm. A perpendicular height $BD=8$ cm meets $AC$ at $D$, and angle $BAD=35\text{°}$. What is angle $BCD$ to 1 decimal place?
